clue.text: Terriers kept in stylish compound

indicators.note: kept in says the soldiers are held inside the word for stylish

parts.note: posh means smart or stylish
Terriers are members of the Territorial Army, TA

explanation.surface: Some dogs are shut up in a fashionable enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' looks like dogs, but it is the old nickname for Territorial Army volunteers, TA. POTASH is the everyday name for potassium compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound, such as the carbonate used in fertiliser.

clue.text: Father joins Hindu sage, leaving mother to carry an item of headgear

indicators.note: to carry says the father holds the next little word inside him

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
taken as written

indicators.note: leaving says the word for mother departs from the sage's title

parts.note: a mahatma is a revered Hindu sage
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A father teams up with an Indian holy man while the mother goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: PA holds AN to make PANA; MAHATMA without MA gives MAHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama hat is a lightweight woven straw hat, a classic piece of summer headwear.

clue.text: Tour operator at first shunned fashionable Italian destination

indicators.note: shunned says a letter is avoided, so it is dropped from the word tour
at first points to the opening letter of operator

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A tour company avoids a trendy holiday spot in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUR without O (operator's first letter) leaves TUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, a place travellers go to.

clue.text: Jumped out of line, alarmed

indicators.note: out of places the jumping word on the outside of the line's letter

parts.note: started means jumped, as in started with surprise

explanation.surface: Someone leapt out of a queue, frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: STARTED goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To be startled is to be suddenly frightened or alarmed.

clue.text: About to sing a couple of notes by south German composer

parts.note: C (circa) means about
to hum is to sing with the lips closed
N is an abbreviation for note, so two of them give a pair of letters

explanation.surface: A singer about to hum a couple of notes next to a southern German composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by south' puts S beside the rest; it comes first here.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a nineteenth-century German Romantic composer.

clue.text: Popular film shown in April, May and June?

definitions.text: Popular film shown in April, May and June?

parts.words: Popular film shown in April, May and June?
parts.note: April, May and June are months but also women's names, so a wall chart of months could picture women; a hit British film had such a premise

explanation.surface: A movie screened over three spring months.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2003 British comedy film featured Women's Institute members posing for a charity calendar; the question mark flags the double reading of the month names.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the months read as girls' names on a calendar, giving the title of a popular film.

clue.text: Besieging US city, Huns will roam free

indicators.note: Besieging means surrounding, so the shuffled tribe goes round the city
will roam says the letters of the tribe wander into a new order

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a US city

explanation.surface: Invading hordes surround an American city and run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roam free' looks like one phrase, but 'will roam' is the anagram signal and 'free' alone is the definition, a verb meaning untie.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlash is to untie or set loose something that was tied down.

clue.text: Causes dismay going round ring twice perched on a horse

indicators.note: perched on in a down clue puts the first part on top of the last
going round says the dismaying verb encircles what follows

parts.note: appals means causes dismay

indicators.note: twice says the ring's letter appears two times

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled by a rider circling a ring twice on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps the verb round two rings; in a down clue 'perched on' sets everything so far above the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: An Appaloosa is a breed of horse with a distinctive spotted coat.

clue.text: 19 appears weird in New York

indicators.note: in says the strange word sits inside the city's initials

parts.note: odd means weird

explanation.surface: Something strange shows up in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 19 across is TWIT, a fool, which is what the definition points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A noddy is an old word for a simpleton, the same sense as the fool of 19.

clue.text: Who invaded Britain? Standard answer: a partnership

parts.note: a norm is a standard
in bridge North and South, NS, form a partnership

explanation.surface: A quiz question about who invaded Britain, and its answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge the players sit as North-South and East-West partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans, under William the Conqueror, invaded Britain in 1066.

clue.text: Condition of boat undermined by showers in east

indicators.note: undermined by says the letters of the following words are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vessel's condition is damaged by eastern rainstorms.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaworthiness is a boat's fitness to put to sea, its condition.

clue.text: Leaf floating on water near girl's flat

indicators.note: near says the flat sits next to the girl

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
a pad is a slang word for a flat

explanation.surface: Something floats near a young woman's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the broad flat leaf of a water lily lying on the surface.

clue.text: Fellow disheartened expressionist painter

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: disheartened says everything but the first and last letters of the next word is removed

explanation.surface: A gloomy man paints in an expressive style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressionist painter' reads as one phrase, but the painter alone is the definition; EXPRESSIONIST loses its innards to give ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Colleague of Greene's travelling companion is a target for criticism

indicators.note: of says the colleague belongs to the aunt, so the aunt comes first

parts.note: Graham Greene's novel Travels with My Aunt has an aunt as the travelling companion, here in the possessive
an ally is a colleague or supporter

explanation.surface: An associate of the novelist's travel partner is open to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a fairground game of throwing at a dummy, hence anyone set up to be attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a figure set up to be pelted, so a person or idea that draws easy criticism.

clue.text: Rider Haggard's principal character was no more original

indicators.note: principal character means the leading letter of Haggard's
original means newly made, so the letters of was no more are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A novelist's leading heroine was no longer innovative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider Haggard' is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, but 'Rider' is the definition; WAS NO MORE rearranged gives ORSEWOMAN after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsewoman is a woman who rides horses, a rider.

clue.text: Restore control, say

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with reins
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Bring back control, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position.

clue.text: Take down name of offending player — reserve

definitions.text: Take down name of offending player
definitions.meaning: in football a referee ... a player by writing the name down
to reserve a seat or table

explanation.surface: A referee records a foul and the player is benched.
explanation.definitionFit: Book means both to note a player's name for a foul and to reserve something in advance.

clue.text: Field marshal supplied clothing, food and drink about middle of month

parts.note: kit means clothing

indicators.note: about says the food-and-drink word surrounds the central letter

parts.note: cheer can mean food and drink, as in good cheer

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of month

explanation.surface: A field marshal was given uniform, rations and drink in mid-month.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEER goes round N, the middle of MONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal, famous from the First World War recruiting poster.

clue.text: Programme dropped ahead of Christmas broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast says the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: shed means dropped and Yule means Christmas, with the shed word first

explanation.surface: A TV show was pulled ahead of the Christmas transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: This relies on the British way of saying the answer, beginning with a sh sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a programme or timetable of planned events.

clue.text: Fool caught without clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the words around wrap the letters within them

explanation.surface: An idiot is found naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without clothes' looks like naked, but 'clothes' means encloses: the letters run across caughT WIThout.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly or foolish person.

clue.text: Get fast car to develop capacity for top performance?

indicators.note: to develop says the letters of the following words grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A driver buys a quick car to boost its performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The performance is on a stage, not a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecraft is skill in theatrical performance, the ability to perform well on stage.

clue.text: Bird left in trap

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A bird is abandoned in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A linnet is a small brown finch.

clue.text: Fine, one incurred by grumpier person in court?

indicators.note: incurred by here means taken in by, so the fine and the one go inside

parts.note: testier means grumpier
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A grumpy person is fined.
explanation.walkthrough: F and I go inside TESTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A testifier is someone who gives evidence, typically a witness in court.

clue.text: Trails bordering bend in river abroad

indicators.note: bordering says the trailing word lies on either side of the bend

parts.note: tags means trails or follows, as in tags along
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: Paths run alongside a bend in a foreign river.
explanation.walkthrough: TAGS goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is a long river in Spain and Portugal, flowing to Lisbon.

clue.text: What did you say about painting in brownish pigment?

indicators.note: about says the questioning word goes round the painting

parts.note: eh is a casual way of asking what someone said
painting is art

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question about a painting in a brown tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal here, not a topic word; earth pigments such as umber are brownish.
explanation.definitionFit: Earths are natural pigments such as umber and sienna, often brownish.

clue.text: Restricted in a way, champion took part in competition

indicators.note: Restricted in says the champion is confined inside the road

parts.note: RD, road, is a way
an ace is a champion

explanation.surface: A champion confined to one route still competed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restricted in' is the container signal; 'a way' is a road, abbreviated RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to compete in a contest of speed.

clue.text: Orphan girl accompanies grey old lady

indicators.note: accompanies says the orphan goes along beside the grey

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie is the famous orphan girl of comics and musicals

explanation.surface: A young orphan goes with an elderly woman with grey hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Grannie is an informal word for a grandmother, an old lady.

clue.text: A small amount of food given to prisoner

parts.note: soup is a food
a con, short for convict, is a prisoner

explanation.surface: A tiny ration is handed to a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon, from French, is a very small amount or trace.

clue.text: Adolescent mostly going round in smart clothing is rather cute

indicators.note: clothing says the smart word wraps around the rest

parts.note: swish means smart or fashionable

indicators.note: going round says the shortened youth is turned to face the other way
mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: A teenager in fashionable clothes looks rather cute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round in smart clothing' reads as a teenager parading in fine clothes, but it hides two steps: a reversal ('going round') and a container ('clothing').
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetish means somewhat sweet, a little cute or charming.

clue.text: Non-stop drinking, principally, with ale all round?

definitions.text: Non-stop drinking, principally, with ale all round?

indicators.note: all round says the ale surrounds the letters picked out

parts.note: beer is ale

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letters of Non-stop and drinking

explanation.surface: A drinking session with endless ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' sets the ale around ND, the first letters picked by 'principally'; the whole clue also describes a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is a drinking spree, so non-stop drinking with plenty of ale.
